web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Price Is What It Is — Reverse DCF, Dilution & Peer Valuation
question: What growth, margin, and multiple assumptions are priced into Yash Highvoltage at ₹1,237.25 (60.15x TTM P/E), and what does fully diluted FY28E fair value show against listed T&D peers?

epigraph.quote: A rich trailing multiple is neither a bargain nor a bubble in isolation; it is a mathematical bet on how long high incremental returns can survive dilution, competition, and trade friction.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Principle

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Reverse DCF & Fully Diluted Enterprise Value at ₹1,237.25

web_blocks.html: Our valuation audit separates two verified market closes. The November 23, 2026 BSE ledger close stands at ₹1,225.50 (Yahoo BSE feed). The live November 25, 2026 TradingView close stands at ₹1,237.25 [19][24]. At ₹1,237.25, Yash carries a basic market cap of ₹3,663.86 crore across 2.9613 crore basic shares [19]. That basic count omits pending dilution from the August 2026 raise and employee options [1][6]. On September 30, 2026, promoters held 53.79% basic equity versus 50.57% fully diluted [6]. That ratio implies 3.150 crore fully diluted shares, capturing all 8.3 lakh Malabar warrants (₹60 crore) plus Employee Stock Option Plan 2025 [1][6].

Across 3.150 crore diluted shares, market cap rises to ₹3,897.3 crore at ₹1,237.25 [6][19]. September 2026 reported net cash is ₹95.0 crore (₹95.6 crore cash versus ₹10.3 crore debt; strict cash less debt is ₹85.3 crore) [1]. Exercising the remaining 75% of Malabar warrants adds ₹45.0 crore of cash [1]. Subtracting ₹140.0 crore of pro-forma net cash leaves a fully diluted Enterprise Value of ₹3,757 crore (versus ₹3,569 crore basic) [1][19]. On trailing results, shares trade at 60.15x P/E and 11.56x P/B [19]. Those multiples rest on 25.04% ROE, 24.52% operating margin, 70.82% sales growth, and 102.67% EPS growth [19].
To measure what today's price demands over ten years, we solve backwards from ₹3,757 crore Enterprise Value. We pair a small-cap industrial discount rate with normalized maintenance free cash flow.

web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹1,237.25 on fully diluted shares, the market prices in ~25%–27% annualized free cash flow compounding for ten straight years with almost no allowance for tariff drag, Jarod delays, or multiple compression [1][19][36].

web_blocks.html: Our Reverse DCF shows zero margin of safety once pending dilution and forensic risks enter the model. Annualizing H1 FY27 revenue (₹194.5 crore) and PAT (₹36.2 crore) implies ₹380–₹400 crore FY27E sales and ₹70–₹74 crore PAT [1][3]. That yields ₹22.22–₹23.49 in diluted EPS, putting shares at 53x–56x fully diluted FY27E earnings [1][6]. Management's FY27 revenue remarks also cite two unreconciled ranges: 40%–45% growth (₹329–₹341 crore) versus ₹360–₹400 crore invoicing [2]. Meanwhile, cumulative FY22–FY26 CFO/PAT was just 49% before H1 FY27's payables-aided rebound [1]. Paying 53x–56x diluted earnings requires flawless execution across a delayed plant ramp, a mid-2027 Swiss supply sunset, and proposed US tariffs [36][38].

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Multiple Rerating Mechanics & Why BSE SME Structure Caps the Multiple

web_blocks.html: Over the twelve months through November 25, 2026, Yash Highvoltage returned +163.27% [19]. Trailing P/E expanded from 25x–30x post-IPO to 60.15x [10][19]. Three operating proofs fueled that rerating. Dry-type RIP bushings reached 86% of H1 FY27 revenue [1]. Gross margin rose 800 bps, from 40.3% in FY24 to 48.3% in H1 FY27 [1]. On November 14, Acuité Ratings certified zero deviation on the ₹151 crore preferential issue, which brought WhiteOak, ValueQuest, Motilal Oswal, and Malabar onto the register [1][6][33].

Yet four fresh forensic facts cap what a disciplined buyer should pay for FY28E earnings. First, Yash listed on BSE SME on December 19, 2024 [10]. BSE's mandatory three-year SME tenure bars Mainboard migration until December 2027, keeping half-yearly reporting and lot-size liquidity friction [10]. Second, promoter-family open-market sales hit 400,000 shares (~₹40.9 crore) across September–November 2026 [34]. That includes Chairman and MD Keyur Shah selling 100,000 shares (~₹12.5 crore) on November 11 and 13 [34]. Third, March 2026's ₹2.10 crore cyber-fraud loss exposed payment-control gaps during rapid growth [7]. Fourth, Jarod trials slipped six months from March 2026 guidance, leaving indigenous core production racing Swiss partner MGC Moser Glaser's mid-2027 sunset with no non-compete bar [1][38].

web_blocks.title: 7.3 Listed Indian T&D Equipment Peer Comparison

web_blocks.html: We compare Yash Highvoltage against five listed Indian T&D peers from the live November 25, 2026 TradingView snapshot. Voltamp Transformers is absent from the November 23 Yahoo ledger, so its metrics come strictly from live TradingView data. The other four large-cap peers appear on both feeds.

web_blocks.caption: Yash Highvoltage vs. Listed Indian T&D Equipment Peers (Live TradingView Snapshot: Nov 25, 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: YASHHV trades at nearly double debt-free transformer peer VOLTAMP (30.88x P/E) and well above SIEMENS (38.72x) and ABB (49.30x), while sitting below large-cap MNC grid leaders CGPOWER (89.26x) and POWERINDIA (110.16x) that enjoy liquid Mainboard floats and multi-product scale [19][21][22][30][31][32].

web_blocks.html: The peer grid highlights a clear divide between valuation and scale [19][21][22][30][31][32]. At the value anchor, Voltamp Transformers (VOLTAMP) trades at ₹9,676.00 (₹9,705 crore market cap) and 30.88x TTM P/E [21]. Voltamp posts a 15.31% operating margin, +17.84% sales growth, and -2.60% trailing EPS growth [21]. Mid-range MNCs Siemens (SIEMENS) at ₹3,581.10 and ABB India (ABB) at ₹7,028.50 trade at 38.72x and 49.30x P/E [30][31]. At the top end, CG Power (CGPOWER) trades at 89.26x P/E (11.59% operating margin), and Hitachi Energy India (POWERINDIA) trades at 110.16x P/E (+51.52% sales growth) [22][32].

Yash earns a real premium over Voltamp. Its 24.52% operating margin, 25.04% ROE, and condenser-bushing moat beat bulk transformer assembly [19][21]. Still, paying 48x–52x forward earnings—above Mainboard MNC ABB (49.30x trailing)—ignores four clear discounts [30]. Yash is a ₹3,664 crore BSE SME micro-cap with ~40%–45% top-5 customer concentration, ₹40.9 crore of recent promoter sales, and direct competition from Hitachi Energy's Halol plant [34][37][39]. A fair normalized FY28E multiple sits at 35x–42x. That grants a 13%–36% quality premium over Voltamp and sits above Siemens, without awarding MNC conglomerate multiples to a single-plant micro-cap [21][31].

web_blocks.title: 7.4 Cycle & Valuation Parallel: Hitachi Energy India (2021–2026)

web_blocks.html: High-voltage grid leaders can hold rich multiples during order booms. Yet even the strongest franchise suffers steep pullbacks when expectations outrun execution. Hitachi Energy India illustrates both sides of that cycle.

web_blocks.mechanism: During India's HVDC and substation buildout, Hitachi Energy India traded persistently between 60x and 110x trailing earnings as its order backlog swelled more than threefold and localized manufacturing lifted margins from trough levels—yet once the stock peaked near ₹38,785, routine digestion pulled shares down over 23% below their 52-week high and below their 30-week average despite +51.5% sales growth.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Compounded >15x from ~₹2,500 (2021) to ₹38,785 high (~12x to ₹29,770 on Nov 25, 2026 at 110.16x TTM P/E), yet sits -23.24% below its 52-week peak and -7.73% below its 30-week SMA (₹32,265) [32].
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: High-voltage scarcity supports premium multiples only while every growth pillar fires cleanly; buying a 60x–110x grid stock near highs leaves investors exposed to sharp 20%–35% multiple resets whenever execution or sector breadth cools.

web_blocks.title: 7.5 Fully Diluted FY28E Valuation Sensitivity & Why 60x Fails the Margin-of-Safety Test

web_blocks.html: We model three FY28E earnings paths across 3.150 crore fully diluted shares (including 8.3 lakh Malabar warrants and ESOP 2025) [6]. In our Base Case, the ₹760+ crore backlog lifts FY28E sales to ₹510 crore [1]. Higher Jarod depreciation, selective customer sharing of core savings, and tariff friction normalize EBITDA margin from 28.1% to 25.5% [1][36]. That delivers ₹90 crore PAT (₹28.57 diluted EPS) [1]. Our Bear Case models ₹440 crore sales and 22.5% EBITDA margin (₹68 crore PAT, ₹21.59 diluted EPS) if Jarod slips past mid-2027 or US tariffs stall exports [36][38]. Our Bull Case models ₹590 crore sales and 27.5% EBITDA margin (₹108 crore PAT, ₹34.29 diluted EPS) on clean Q3 FY27 commissioning and US tariff exemptions [1][36].

web_blocks.caption: Fully Diluted FY28E PAT vs. Forward P/E Matrix (3.150 Cr Diluted Shares; Return vs. Live CMP ₹1,237.25)
web_blocks.takeaway: On 3.150 Cr fully diluted shares, realistic Base Case FY28E earnings (₹90 Cr PAT; ₹28.57 FD EPS) at a peer-aligned 42x multiple equal ₹1,200 per share (-3.0% below live CMP ₹1,237.25) [6][19].

web_blocks.html: That matrix settles the valuation question cleanly. Even at a generous 42x forward FY28E multiple—36% above Voltamp (30.88x) and above Siemens (38.72x)—fair value on ₹90 crore PAT across 3.150 crore diluted shares is exactly ₹1,200 per share [6][21][31]. That sits -3.0% below the November 25 close of ₹1,237.25 [19]. Hitting the prior dossier's ₹1,550 target on diluted shares would require 54.3x Base FY28E earnings, or 45.2x flawless Bull Case earnings. Against the live support shelf (₹1,161.90–₹1,197.28) and stop (₹949.50), a ₹1,200 Base Target offers just 0.01:1 reward-to-risk from ₹1,197.28 (₹2.72 upside versus ₹247.78 risk) [19][24]. That fails our 1.50:1 asymmetry hurdle by a wide margin.

Valuation Trigger: Re-underwrite only if shares reset to ₹950–₹1,020 (33x–36x FY28E diluted EPS, restoring >=1.50:1 asymmetry). Otherwise, wait for H2 FY27 proof of commercial indigenous RIP cores before mid-2027, US tariff exemptions, DSO below 60 days, and zero further promoter sales lifting FY28E PAT above ₹110 crore.

book_paragraphs: Once you and I complete a forensic audit of the factory floor, supply chain, and governance footnotes, we finally earn the right to open the valuation ledger. And when we look at Yash Highvoltage in late November 2026—closing at ₹1,225.50 on the November 23 BSE ledger and ₹1,237.25 on the live November 25 TradingView tape—the valuation tells a very different story than the one investors saw before our blind-spot audit.

At first glance, the headline screen looks familiar: a ₹3,663.86 crore basic market capitalization and a 60.15x trailing twelve-month price-to-earnings ratio. Momentum traders shrug off 60x because H1 FY27 revenue jumped 95% year-on-year to ₹194.5 crore and net profit surged 165% to ₹36.2 crore. Value investors walk away at 60x without reading a single footnote. Neither shortcut works. To price Yash honestly, we must account for every diluted share, every new competitor factory, every rupee of promoter selling, and the November 25 US tariff proposal.

book_subsections.title: Counting Every Share: Why Basic Market Cap Understates the True Price Tag
paragraphs: Most surface-level valuation notes divide market cap by today's basic share count and stop there. That shortcut misses meaningful dilution sitting right on the September 30, 2026 shareholding disclosure. At ₹1,237.25 per share, Yash's basic market cap of ₹3,663.86 crore implies roughly 2.9613 crore basic shares. Yet in August 2026, alongside 12.6 lakh equity shares, Yash issued 8.3 lakh convertible warrants worth ₹60 crore to Malabar India Fund (25% paid upfront, with an 18-month exercise window) and later extended its Employee Stock Option Plan 2025 exercise period from two years to four years.

Look directly at the September 30 filing: promoters held 53.79% of basic equity, but 50.57% on a fully diluted basis. That ratio implies roughly 6.4% dilution—lifting the true economic share count to approximately 3.150 crore shares. Multiply 3.150 crore shares by ₹1,237.25, and the fully diluted market cap is ₹3,897.3 crore. Even after crediting ₹95.0 crore of September 2026 net cash plus ₹45.0 crore of remaining cash inflow when Malabar converts its warrants, the fully diluted Enterprise Value stands at ₹3,757 crore.

That extra 18.9 lakh shares may sound small in percentage terms, yet when a stock trades at 60 times trailing earnings, a 6.4% dilution adjustment immediately trims per-share fair value by nearly ₹80 before you even touch the operating forecast.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: When warrants are deeply in the money—Malabar's ₹60 crore warrants strike near ₹723 against a ₹1,237 share price—pretending they will not convert is financial make-believe. Always underwrite on fully diluted shares.

book_subsections.title: What the Reverse DCF Demands Over the Next Ten Years
paragraphs: Now let us ask a simple Reverse Discounted Cash Flow question: what must Yash Highvoltage achieve over the next decade to justify a ₹3,757 crore fully diluted Enterprise Value? Because Yash is a ₹3,664 crore micro-cap bound to the BSE SME exchange until at least December 2027—carrying lot-size liquidity friction, half-yearly financial reporting, recent promoter selling, and a March 2026 cyber-fraud control lapse—we apply a 13.0% cost of equity and a 5.5% terminal growth rate.

Annualizing H1 FY27's ₹36.2 crore net profit puts full-year FY27E earnings around ₹70 to ₹74 crore, or ₹22.22 to ₹23.49 per fully diluted share. On a maintenance free cash flow base of ₹54 to ₹58 crore (excluding greenfield Jarod expansion capex), today's ₹3,757 crore Enterprise Value requires Yash to compound free cash flow at roughly 25% to 27% every single year for ten straight years. That means reaching ₹700 to ₹800 crore in annual sales by FY31 while holding net margins above 17% and keeping working capital tightly contained.

Could Yash pull that off? Perhaps, if everything breaks right. Remember, however, that cumulative FY22 to FY26 operating cash flow was only 49% of net profit before H1 FY27's payables-boosted jump to 125%, and management itself gave two unreconciled FY27 revenue figures—40% to 45% growth versus ₹360 to ₹400 crore of invoicing. Paying 53x to 56x fully diluted FY27E earnings leaves zero buffer if even one link in the chain slips.

book_subsections.title: Four Forensic Ceilings on the Exit Multiple
paragraphs: When we re-underwrote Yash Highvoltage from scratch without anchoring to our earlier 45x–50x multiple band, four new forensic facts forced a sober reset of what multiple the market will pay two years from now.

First is the BSE SME structural ceiling. Yash listed on BSE SME on December 19, 2024. Under exchange rules requiring a three-year SME tenure before Mainboard migration, Yash cannot move to the Mainboard until December 2027. That preserves half-yearly statutory reporting opacity and restricts broad mutual-fund liquidity for another full year. Second is promoter supply: between September and November 2026, promoter-family members sold 400,000 shares worth roughly ₹40.9 crore on the open market—including Chairman and Managing Director Keyur Shah selling 100,000 shares worth about ₹12.5 crore on November 11 and 13, trimming his direct stake from 50.58% to 50.24%. Founders are entitled to diversify, yet recurring open-market sales right near 52-week highs signal that insiders do not view 60x earnings as undervalued.

Third is execution and competitive compression. Jarod's commissioning timeline already slipped roughly six months from early post-IPO expectations of March 2026, leaving end-to-end indigenous RIP core production racing against Swiss partner MGC Moser Glaser's mid-2027 supply-exclusivity sunset—which carries no non-compete bar. Meanwhile, Hitachi Energy broke ground on an integrated dry-bushing plant right in Halol, Vadodara to quadruple India's EHV and UHV dry-bushing capacity, while Trench/HSP opened a Charlotte, North Carolina plant in July 2026 and agreed to be acquired by GE Vernova for $9.0 billion in October 2026. Fourth is trade policy: on November 25, 2026, the U.S. Trade Representative proposed Section 301 tariffs of up to 25% on all Indian goods (17% with a bilateral agreement, compared with 15% caps for Europe and Switzerland), directly threatening the export margin premium Yash planned to capture across its 27-state US sales network.

book_subsections.title: Benchmarking Against Five Listed Indian T&D Peers
paragraphs: Lining Yash up against five live listed Indian T&D peers from the November 25 TradingView snapshot puts its 60.15x multiple in sharp perspective. At the conservative end sits Voltamp Transformers at ₹9,676.00 and 30.88x trailing earnings—a clean, debt-free domestic transformer manufacturer generating a 15.31% operating margin, though currently trapped in a Stage 4 downtrend with -2.60% trailing EPS growth. Next sit two Mainboard global MNC franchises: Siemens India at 38.72x P/E (₹1.28 lakh crore market cap) and ABB India at 49.30x P/E (₹1.45 lakh crore market cap). At the top sit CG Power at 89.26x P/E and Hitachi Energy India at 110.16x P/E—massive, multi-division Mainboard powerhouses with deep institutional liquidity.

Yash's 24.52% trailing operating margin and 25.04% ROE clearly beat Voltamp's transformer-assembly margins, justifying a solid premium over 30.88x. Yet paying 48x to 54x forward FY28E earnings for a single-product, ₹3,664 crore BSE SME micro-cap—where top-five customers represent roughly 40% to 45% of sales, Indian PLI incentives remain unapproved, and a ₹2.10 crore cyber-fraud loss just hit FY26—is stretching peer logic past its breaking point. Bridging between Voltamp (30.88x) and ABB (49.30x), an honest, quality-adjusted FY28E Base multiple for Yash sits at 42x—a 36% premium to Voltamp and modestly above Siemens.

book_subsections.title: The Hitachi Energy India Lesson: Even 110x Grid Winners Reset Violently
paragraphs: Consider the cautionary mirror of Hitachi Energy India. Between 2021 and early 2026, Hitachi Energy proved that high-voltage grid scarcity can sustain 60x to 110x trailing earnings far longer than skeptics expect, compounding more than fifteenfold from ~₹2,500 to a ₹38,785 high. Yet look at where Hitachi Energy sits on November 25, 2026: even with +51.52% trailing revenue growth and +66.29% EPS growth, the stock trades at ₹29,770 (~12x its 2021 base)—23.24% below its 52-week peak and 7.73% below its 30-week moving average.

That is the unforgiving physics of expensive industrial multiples. When a stock already discounts three years of perfection, the business does not have to fail for shareholders to lose 25% of their capital; growth merely has to pause or margins have to normalize by two hundred basis points.

book_subsections.title: Running the Honest FY28E Sensitivity Grid
paragraphs: Now put our three FY28E earnings cases through the 3.150 crore fully diluted share count. In our Base Case, domestic grid demand converts Yash's ₹760+ crore backlog into roughly ₹510 crore of FY28E revenue, while higher Jarod depreciation, domestic competition from Hitachi Halol, and customer sharing of localization savings bring EBITDA margins down slightly from H1 FY27's peak 28.1% to a healthy 25.5%. That delivers ₹90 crore of FY28E net profit, or ₹28.57 per fully diluted share.

Multiply ₹28.57 by our peer-aligned 42x multiple, and Base Case fair value lands at exactly ₹1,200 per share—3.0% below the November 25 live price of ₹1,237.25. At 35x, Base fair value drops to ₹1,000 (-19.2%); at Voltamp's 30x multiple, it falls to ₹857 (-30.7%). In our Bear Case, if Jarod's indigenous RIP cores slip past MGC Moser Glaser's mid-2027 sunset or US Section 301 tariffs stall export conversion, FY28E PAT drops toward ₹68 crore (₹21.59 diluted EPS), pulling fair value at 35x down to ₹756—our ₹750 Bear Target (-39.4%). Only in our Bull Case—where Jarod commissions smoothly in Q3 FY27, bushings win US tariff exemptions, and FY28E PAT hits ₹108 crore (₹34.29 diluted EPS) at 45x—does the stock reach ₹1,545 (+24.9%).

Check what that Base Target of ₹1,200 means for our technical support shelf. The live Stage 2 support band sits between ₹1,161.90 and ₹1,197.28, with structural invalidation at ₹949.50. Buying at the top of support (₹1,197.28) risks ₹247.78 per share to capture just ₹2.72 of upside to ₹1,200—a 0.01-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio. Even at the bottom of support (₹1,161.90), upside to ₹1,200 is only 0.18-to-1. To earn a genuine 1.50-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio against our ₹1,200 Base Target, Yash would need to reset into the ₹950 to ₹1,020 price zone—well below its current Stage 2 shelf. That is why valuation discipline overrides enthusiasm today.
